The samples should now be checked for successful amplification, contamination in negatives and any secondary banding. Gel electrophoresis will achieve this, but digital systems like the Qiagen Qiaxcel will do this and facilitate equalisation by generating amplicon-specific DNA concentrations (see the robotics-based protocol step-case).

Equalisation is more effective than normalisation, but requires amplicon concentration data. Both can be time and labour intensive though, so can be skipped if time restricted for large-scale projects, although at the expense of data recovery and evenness. The robotics-based protocol step-case goes through equalisation using a Qiagen Qiaxcel, but this process could also be emulated by bead-cleaning all of the samples individually (as per the bead clean in the equalisation protocol following the pooling steps), and then using a Qubit fluorometer (or similar) to quantify the concentrations of amplicons. Samples could then be pooled based on Qubit concentrations, and will then be ready for library preparation (no further bead cleaning necessary unless the overall concentration is low and you would like to concentrate the library by eluting into a smaller volume). If doing that, it is crucial that the Qubit measurements are taken after bead cleaning so that primers and primer dimers do not contribute to the DNA concentrations used for pooling. If the PCRs were replicated (i.e., each sample run multiple times for each PCR primer pair used), these can be merged together into one plate at this point, or carried forward separately. Keeping the replicates separate increases the number of libraries to prepare and sequence later, but better facilitates inconsistencies between samples. To merge triplicates, assuming use of 10 µL reaction volumes, pipette 8 µL from each well of two of the three plates into the corresponding well of the third. Briefly centrifuge the merged plate to move the oil to the top of the product again. To avoid pipetting oil from the oil-sealed PCR products, plunge the pipette to the first stop and fully insert the pipette tip into the bottom of the well, then release sharply. The PCR product will be taken up quickly, whereas the relatively viscous oil will be taken up slowly, thus being outcompeted by the PCR product.

steps.title: Prepare Soil Samples
steps.instruction: Collect a small (< 2 g) sample of soil using a sterilized corer, collection tube, or gloved hand. Decontaminate tools and surfaces between samples with Chemgene, rinsing with molecular biology-grade water and 100% ethanol.

steps.title: Homogenize Soil and Extract Lysate
steps.instruction: Combine soil with TNES lysis buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl, 52 mM NaCl, 10 mM EDTA, 10% SDS).

substeps.instruction: Add up to 2 g of soil to the TNES buffer.
Add three 2-3 mm steel beads (if using machinery beads, bake at 250 °C for 12 hours to remove oil).
Homogenize at 1750 rpm for 4 minutes in a grinder/lyser (e.g., GenoGrinder).
Centrifuge at 2000 x g for 2 minutes to separate solid particulate matter from the lysate.

steps.title: Filter and Store Lysate
steps.instruction: Separate the supernatant from physical material using a filter plate.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 2000 x g for 2 minutes.
Discard the filter plate. Samples can be stored at -20 °C at this stage.

steps.title: Prepare Larvae Lysate
steps.instruction: Process larvae samples to obtain lysate.

substeps.instruction: Grind larvae in a Geno/Grinder 2010 at full speed (1750 RPM) for 4 minutes; repeat if not fully homogenized.
Centrifuge at 4,000 g for 2 minutes.
Remove ball bearings using a magnet.
Add 1 mL of Proteinase Buffer master mix (Lysis Buffer 2: pH 9, 120 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris-Hcl, 20 mM EDTA, 3% SDS; and Proteinase K at 10 mg/mL) to the lysate and vortex.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight (12-16 hours).
Centrifuge at 4000 x g for 4 minutes.

steps.title: Process and Archive Lysate
steps.instruction: Separate and store the supernatant for downstream use.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of supernatant to a clean 2.2 mL deep-well 96-well plate for archiving.
Centrifuge the remaining lysate at 2000 x g for 4 minutes.
Transfer 200 μL of the supernatant to a clean 2.2 mL deep-well 96-well plate; store remaining lysate at -20 °C.

steps.title: DNA Extraction via Magnetic Beads (Kingfisher Apex)
steps.instruction: Perform automated DNA extraction using the Kingfisher Apex or magnetic racks.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a sample plate: add 60 µL lysate, 120 µL 1.5X GITC buffer (6 M GITC, 75 mM Tris-HCl, 3% sarkosyl, 30 mM EDTA, 0.15% antifoam), 120 µL 1 mg/mL SeraMag Speed Beads in TE (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA), and 240 µL isopropanol. Mix by pipetting or vortexing (1500 rpm, 1 min).
Prepare reagent plates: two plates with 400 µL 80% ethanol per well, one plate with 400 µL isopropanol per well, and one elution plate with 100 µL molecular biology grade water per well.
Bind DNA: Mix beads at medium speed for 5 min, followed by a slow post-mix for 5 min. Collect beads in three 1-sec collections.
Wash 1: Release beads into isopropanol, mix for 1 min at medium speed, and collect in three 1-sec collections.
Wash 2: Release beads into 80% ethanol, mix for 1 min at medium speed, and collect in three 1-sec collections. Repeat this process three times across separate ethanol plates.
Dry: Dry beads above the well for 2 min.
Elute: Release beads into elution plate, mix for 2 min at fast speed with a slow post-mix for 3 min, and collect in four 20-sec collections.
Store eluted DNA at -20 °C.

steps.title: DNA Extraction via Spin Column (Manual)
steps.instruction: Extract DNA using silica membrane spin columns.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Protein Denaturation Buffer (5 M Guanidine HCl, pH ~7) and mix with 100% ethanol (220 μL each per sample).
Add 200 μL of supernatant from previous steps into the denaturation mix.
Load ~600 μL of sample solution onto a 96-well DNA membrane spin column; centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1 min (or 10 min if centrifuge is slower) and discard flow-through.
Wash 1: Add 500 μL Wash Buffer 1, centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1 min (or 5 min if slower), and discard flow-through.
Wash 2: Add 500 μL Wash Buffer 2 (pH ~7, 70% Ethanol, 10 mM Tris-Hcl, H2O), centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 3 min (or 15 min if slower), and discard flow-through.
Transfer the spin column plate to a 0.5 mL DNA collection plate, ensuring the base does not touch the liquid.
Elute: Add 200 μL Elution Buffer (pH ~7, 10 mM Tris-Hcl, H2O) directly to the membrane, incubate at room temperature for 5 min, and centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1 min (or 5 min if slower).

steps.title: PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Amplify target DNA using tagged primers.

substeps.instruction: Design plate layout including negative controls (each row/column), positive controls, and blank controls.
Prepare PCR mastermix for 25 µL reaction volumes.
Prepare a primer plate with tagged forward (8 types) and reverse (12 types) primers at 5 µM concentration.
Add 22.75 µL hot-start Taq polymerase/water master mix and 1.25 µL primer mix to each well.
Add 1 µL DNA to sample/positive control wells and 1 µL molecular grade water to negative controls.
Add one drop (~20 µL) of mineral oil to each well to prevent evaporation.
Briefly centrifuge and run the PCR program in a thermocycler using appropriate annealing temperatures.

steps.title: Equimolar Pooling
steps.instruction: Pool PCR products to achieve equal representation of samples.

substeps.instruction: Calculate pooling volumes by dividing the maximum concentration in the plate by the concentration of each individual sample.
Pool calculated volumes in microliters. For negative controls, pool the average volume of the samples. For blanks, pool nothing.
If volume exceeds available total, pool the total available. If variation is high, halve all values to facilitate pooling of dilute samples.

steps.title: Library Purification (SPRI)
steps.instruction: Purify pooled PCR products using SPRI beads.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1X SPRI bead solution: Wash 1 mL Sera-Mag SpeedBeads twice with TE+Tween buffer (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA, 0.05% Tween 20, pH 8.0), then add 20 mL 50% PEG.
Add 20 µL of 1X SPRI beads (or volume equivalent to available PCR product) to a 96-well plate.
Add 20 µL PCR product (avoiding oil), vortex (1500 rpm, 1 min), and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Place on magnetic stand for 5 min, remove all but 5 µL of supernatant.
Wash twice with 200 µL 80% ethanol per well.
Air-dry beads until they transition from 'glossy' to 'matte'.
Add 11 µL molecular grade water, shake (1500 rpm, 1 min), and incubate for 5 min.
Place on magnetic stand for 5 min and remove 10 µL of supernatant as the final library.

steps.title: Final Library Quantification
steps.instruction: Quantify the final library concentration (e.g., Qubit dsDNA assay) and prepare for sequencing (Oxford Nanopore or Illumina) based on provider requirements (fmol/µL).
